summary: Rechecked 42 layers, 181 targets and all 199 citation occurrences. One medium finding: the audit overlooks Tau Ceti’s existing smooth discrete representation category and dictionary. The enhanced derived/v-stack comparisons remain missing; no layer is promoted to built.
checked: Read accepted AUDIT-21 and REV-AUDIT-21, all five complete roadmap documents and their stage extracts. Reconciled the audit brief with all 42 audited layers and 181 target records: three built, six partly built and 33 not built; 111 absent, 41 partial, one mathlib and 28 tauceti target labels. This worker neither authored nor reviewed AUDIT-21.

Read all 199 citation occurrences, resolving to 177 distinct declarations, at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 and Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Retained multiline statements, structure fields, local hypotheses and internal assignments, and opened necessary definition bodies and inductive constructors. Verified all 101 cited source files against pinned Git blobs; additional evidence brought that set to 129 files. Cited declarations are not axioms; checked files have no sorry/admit outside comments. Separately verified the hashes and same scan for all 52 files of the CFSG directory. No Lean compilation was performed.

Rechecked the 152 absent/partial targets by searching the declaration index first and pinned Lean files second, in 20 topic groups and a focused smooth-discrete follow-up. Covered loop/Grassmannian geometry, perfect and v-geometry, line-bundle positivity, perverse/Satake/fusion theory, exceptional operations, dual groups/Tannaka, shtukas, smooth representations, ramification/cocycles, parameter schemes/invariants, good filtrations, enhanced and solid/lisse categories, CFSG carriers/comparisons/assembly/pinnings and descent. Search misses are bounded evidence, not proofs of nonexistence.

Checked all 26 duplicate-lead entries against the full descriptions of their 16 distinct owner stages, and verified those descriptions match the corresponding complete source-document sections. Consulted accepted restructuring context for local versus global shtukas, coefficient-category imports, bundle geometry and reductive-group suppliers. Overlap leads and deliberate comparisons were not treated as duplicate proofs solely because they share terminology.

For CFSG, read all index constructors and exclusions, carrier choices and the B2/C2 adapter, ordinary versus half-Frobenius equations, the derived-central-quotient construction and universe lowering. Inspected the 26 presentation records, their source metadata and recorded source-to-Lean/permutation comparison evidence, including the Monster central relator and Baby Monster extra relations. These are statement/construction milestones; finiteness and simplicity of the candidates are not required. Existing external computations were inspected as recorded provenance, not rerun or claimed as new Lean proofs.

Challenged false-positive searches with the nonabelian Cech H1 file, function-field place ramification, binomial power series, Fontaine period-ring definitions, formal smoothness, the known-Hopf-algebra Tannaka reconstruction, generic toral symmetry and the solid-module TODOs. None of those supplies the missing Weil/parameter-stack, geometric Satake or enhanced coefficient endpoint. The smooth discrete category does contradict the audit’s blanket absence claim and is the single finding.
Refreshed all guarded inputs to main 470336c5e85deb65341ede42881e2798f13a6e4f: no acquired input changed. Submitted only the two authorized red-team deliverables.

findings.claim: The repeated blanket claim that smooth representations of p-adic or locally pro-p groups are not defined in either library overlooks Tau Ceti’s smooth discrete coefficient categories. This is existing foundation for the comparison, although neither the enhanced derived category nor the geometric equivalence is supplied by it.
findings.evidence: At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/SmoothDiscrete.lean#L245-L258 defines TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete on TopRep R G by discreteness of the module and openness of every point stabilizer. Lines 531–560 define TauCeti.SmoothDiscreteTopRep as the full subcategory and TauCeti.DiscreteRep as discrete modules with a continuous G-action and scalar action; lines 580–585 give equivariant linear maps as morphisms. Lines 646–687 define TauCeti.discreteRepEquivSmoothTopRep : DiscreteRep R G ≌ SmoothDiscreteTopRep R G for an arbitrary topological group G. The hypotheses do not restrict G to a compact or profinite group. With a discrete coefficient ring, scalar continuity is automatic for discrete modules, so these definitions apply to the torsion coefficient setting of VS4. The declaration index locates these names at lines 254, 537, 550 and 678; their full statements, fields, definition bodies and section assumptions were read. The file matches pinned Git blob 456ca497a722465b26ceca5a35cbea2009bf9e09 and has no sorry/admit outside comments. Its own roadmap paragraph explicitly leaves the categorical limit/subobject/quotient API unfinished.
findings.fix: Retain HS3 targets[2] as absent, VS4 targets[0] as partial, and the two layer verdicts as not built: their geometric and enhanced derived comparisons remain missing. Replace the blanket absence sentences in both notes and the VS summary with an account of the existing smooth discrete predicate, category and categorical dictionary. Add TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete, TauCeti.SmoothDiscreteTopRep and TauCeti.discreteRepEquivSmoothTopRep from SmoothDiscrete.lean:254,537,678 as related declarations for VS4 targets[0] and, if recording the coefficient input there, HS3 targets[2]. Distinguish this existing ordinary category from the still-unbuilt abelian/derived/enhanced API, compact induction, admissibility and v-stack equivalence; do not infer any of those results from the dictionary.
